problem.title: Three reasons your team tools never stick.
problem.p1d: A shared board has no idea who reports to whom. You end up replaying <hl>the hierarchy by hand</hl>, as access rights, and it's wrong the day after the first reorg.
problem.p2d: A role changes, a team splits, a project moves to someone else. <hl>With rigid tools, every change means reconfiguring.</hl> You end up adapting the tool to the change, instead of just moving forward.
problem.p3t: No one can see who's doing what
problem.p3d: Without visibility into who's doing what, a project starts <hl>without knowing if it's even feasible</hl>. You find out midway, once it's too late.

pyramid.title: Invite your team. The org chart draws itself.
pyramid.subtitle: Everyone joins with the Cosmo account they already have, and <hl>you attach them to their manager</hl>. Then group them into teams: those teams carry the projects, the objectives and the statistics.
pyramid.g1d: By email, by code, by link or from your Cosmo contacts. The person joins with the account they already have, straight into their place in the org chart and their teams.
pyramid.g2d: Each member has a single manager. That link decides by default what they see and what they can do, and you adjust right by right when you need to.
pyramid.g3d: Create as many teams as you need, and put whoever you want in them. One person can belong to several teams.
pyramid.b1d: A manager sees their whole subtree: their teams, their projects, their objectives, their statistics. Nothing to tick, nothing to maintain.
pyramid.b2d: Open anyone's profile from the org chart: their current tasks, their workload, their calendar, their contribution.
pyramid.b3t: Put a slot in their calendar
pyramid.b3d: A manager creates, moves and edits events in the calendar of the people reporting to them. Anything they marked as personal stays private: only the slot shows.
pyramid.b4d: Change who a member reports to, and their scope follows: what they see, who they manage. Nothing to reconfigure by hand.

projects.title: Create your projects, assign them at any scale.
projects.subtitle: A project's tasks follow its team. Assign them to whoever you want, one person or several: they simply land in <hl>everyone's personal Cosmo</hl>, no new tool to open.
projects.p1t: To one person, to several, to a whole team
projects.p1d: You assign to anyone within your scope. A task can have <hl>several assignees at once</hl>, or split into <hl>subtasks</hl>, each given to someone.
projects.p2d: The list for task detail, the timeline to see deadlines coming, the portfolio to compare status, lead and progress across all your projects.
projects.p3d: Comment, mention anyone. They get notified, with a badge until they've read it.

execution.title: Track execution, not just deadlines.
execution.subtitle: <hl>Every task carries a status</hl> and can block another. The timeline computes the critical path: the chain where the slightest delay pushes back delivery.
execution.p1t: Every team task, in one table
execution.p1d: The Tasks tab gathers the tasks of every project in your scope: presets (overdue, this week, blocked), shared lists, sorting and grouping, as a list or a board.
execution.p2d: To do, in progress, in review, blocked, done. The status pill shows everywhere: in the table, the board, the timeline. A task in review is approved or sent back in one click.
execution.p3d: Link a task to the ones that must finish before it. Cosmo computes the critical path: the chain of tasks where the smallest delay pushes back delivery. Everything else has slack.

okr.title: Set your objectives, at every scale.
okr.subtitle: An organisation objective breaks down into team OKRs, each OKR into numeric key results. <hl>Every team sees how its work feeds the shared objective</hl>.
okr.orgExample: Make Nova Studio a reference in independent branding
okr.team1Objective: Make every identity delivered a reference in its industry
okr.team2Objective: Build an acquisition engine that no longer relies on word of mouth
okr.team3Objective: Become the agency clients know they can count on
okr.b1: Every team OKR attaches to the organisation objective that gives it meaning.
okr.b2: A key result is a number to hit, not a vague intention.
okr.b3: An objective can be visible to the whole company, to some teams, or only to the people you pick.

progress.title: Track how everyone is progressing.
progress.subtitle: Activity reports answer the Monday morning question: <hl>what moved forward, and thanks to whom</hl>. Readable for the whole company or one team, by day, week or month.
progress.p1t: What moved forward, day after day
progress.p1d: Every night, Cosmo records what the company and each team did: completed tasks, projects and OKRs that progressed, events held.
progress.p2d: The detail per person, tasks completed and events held, so work gets recognised rather than guessed.
progress.p3d: On each team's page, open and overdue tasks for every member. A task is reassigned by drag and drop, before the steering meeting rather than during it.
progress.overviewBody: The home screen of the company space: what's waiting for you (tasks to approve, mentions, people you're blocking), your workload for the week, your calendar and your key results. You approve without leaving the screen. That is where <hl>the day starts</hl>.

more.title: And everything that helps once the team is on board.
more.subtitle: The five steps set up the structure. Here is what saves time <hl>when Cosmo runs every day</hl>, already in the product, included in every tier.
more.f1d: Thirteen rights set member by member, from creating projects to inviting people, plus a chosen assignment scope. An admin always keeps control.
more.f2d: Lead, contributor or viewer: each project decides who steers it, who works on it and who follows it without touching it.
more.f3d: Its lead, its colour, its projects, its key results and each member's workload, in one place.
more.f4d: Schedule a meeting for a whole team in three steps: who, when, details. The slot lands in everyone's calendar.
more.f5d: Right after creating the company: first invitations, first team, first project, without hunting for where to click.
more.f6d: Start from a template (client onboarding, product launch, sprint) or duplicate an existing project with its tasks.
more.f7t: Projects that wait on each other
more.f7d: A project can depend on another. The portfolio shows "blocked by" as soon as the chain tightens.
more.f8d: Select several tasks to assign, move, change status or complete them in one go. Same for members.
more.f9d: Overdue, this week, blocked: one click. Team lists are shared, and a filter can be sent as a plain link.
more.f10d: Ctrl K searches the whole company: projects, tasks, objectives, people. Only what you're allowed to see.
more.f11d: When a task is created or changes status, Cosmo assigns it, changes its priority or status, or notifies the right people.
more.f12d: Your task events go to Slack, or to your own service as signed JSON. Never an email address or a description.
more.f13d: Projects, tasks, objectives, teams and members exported as CSV whenever you want. Your data is never locked in.
more.f14d: Type by type, choose what notifies you in the app or by email, with a daily digest of what you haven't read.
more.f15t: Your KRs in your personal Cosmo
more.f15d: A company key result you own also shows up in your personal OKRs. One place to follow what matters.
more.f16d: Every governance action (members, teams, projects, rights) is recorded and kept for a year, viewable and exportable by admins.
more.f17d: Verify your company's domain through DNS, then only accept invitations to those addresses.
more.f18d: Invite a contractor for thirty days: their access ends on its own, without anyone having to remember.
more.f19d: When someone leaves, an assistant hands over their tasks, direct reports and key results. Or simply suspend their access.
more.f20d: A deleted task or objective stays in the trash for thirty days, with its history, and comes back exactly as it was.

security.title: The questions your committee will ask.
security.subtitle: We answer them here, <hl>before they block the rollout</hl>.
security.s1d: Access rules <hl>live in the database, not in the code shown on screen</hl>. No one can bypass them by tampering with a request.
security.s2d: A manager sees the team projects and tasks in their scope. A member's habits, calendar and personal tasks <hl>stay invisible to their management chain</hl>.
security.s3d: No data is ever resold. <hl>Account deletion is real, not symbolic</hl>, and every retention period is written down.
security.s4t: Leaving is as easy as joining
security.s4d: Ownership transfer, a member's departure with their work handed over, deleting the organisation: it all takes a few clicks, <hl>no support ticket needed</hl>.

faq.title: Organisation questions
faq.q1: Do my teammates need to create a new account?
faq.a1: No. A member joins your organisation with the Cosmo account they already have, by email, code or invitation link. Their personal space stays separate and belongs to them.
faq.q2: Can a manager see their team's personal tasks?
faq.a2: No. The management scope covers team work: projects, assigned tasks, OKRs, collective statistics. A member's personal tasks, habits and calendar are never exposed to their management chain.
faq.q3: Can two teams work without seeing each other?
faq.a3: Yes, that is the default. Two sibling branches of the org chart are partitioned, and the rule is enforced in the database, not merely hidden in the interface.
faq.q4: What happens if we go past a tier?
faq.a4: You can't invite past your tier until you raise it. But no member is ever removed, and nothing is lost if you step back down afterwards.
faq.q5: Can we try without committing the company?
faq.a4Free: Nothing blocks you today: during the launch offer every tier is free and you can invite as many people as you want. Once billing is switched on, you will no longer be able to invite past your tier until you raise it — but no member is ever removed, and nothing is lost if you step back down.
faq.a5: Yes. Create an organisation of up to five members, free and without a credit card. It is the complete product, not a crippled version.
